summary: Calibration found a real cross-lane behavioral break, so nothing was published. Migrated (Angular 16.2) silently discards a typed translation: textarea.ng-dirty set in both lanes, but app-normalized-message-input stays ng-pristine, undo never enables (>11s) and the exported XLIFF carries state=final with the ORIGINAL text; baseline (Angular 5) propagates within ~200ms. App source is a faithful .debounceTime->.pipe(debounceTime) translation, so this is a runtime regression invisible to both build lanes. Landed real measured journey corrections (filter-label selectors, reviewer-half semantics, download settle, debounce anchor); tsc and lint clean.
open_questions: Migrated lane loses typed translations: the component's debounced form.valueChanges -> propagateChange never reaches the outer formControlName control under Angular 16.2, while the era lane fires it in ~200ms. Is this repaired by a migration capability (outside this unit's contract) or published as a recorded behavioral difference? Publishing this vertical green is impossible until that is decided.

The RED record under evidence/runs/angular-tiny-translator-v0-12-0/ was not written (wall clock). Re-cut a small unit to drive both lanes through a u19d-style record driver; the discriminator is mechanical: the journey's settled-state wait on '#translation button[mat-icon-button]' losing 'disabled' passes on baseline and times out on migrated.

Second, still-uncalibrated divergence: the baseline lane clears the editor-commit wait then fails at 'All units' with expected 3 / observed 2 (the untranslated count), suggesting the TranslationFileView is reconstructed after the reviewer commit. Needs one baseline calibration pass with stage-labelled probes.

Core schema amendments (observerFinalization.workerEvents, refusedServiceWorker shape, recorded-amendment list, core receipt test updates) were not attempted, since they should follow a settled journey.
